input: A defect-reduction project was carried out on a filling line, and over the course of one quarter it succeeded in cutting the reject rate from 4.2% to 2%. At 193k units per year, this change avoids about 4246 rejected units per year, which represents a meaningful improvement in the line's performance. It is worth noting, however, that the quarter in question included a planned shutdown, and the rates are not adjusted for it. This means the comparison is not entirely clean: the shutdown may have influenced the measured rates in ways that have not been separated out, and the annual saving is calculated as though the quarterly rates applied across the whole year at the stated volume. Nevertheless, the direction of the change is clear, and the project demonstrates that sustained attention to reject rates can deliver substantial benefits in avoided waste over time. Even so, the reported change is substantial, and the project illustrates the value of measuring reject performance carefully before and after an intervention of this kind. Further monitoring over a longer period, ideally including quarters without interruptions, would help to establish whether the improved rate can be sustained in ordinary operation, and would give a much firmer basis for projecting the annual benefit with confidence.
target: A defect-reduction project on a filling line cut the reject rate from 4.2% to 2% over one quarter. At 193k units per year the change avoids about 4246 rejected units per year. The quarter included a planned shutdown; the rates are not adjusted for it. The avoided figure is computed on the annual volume at the two quarterly rates, and the shutdown sits inside that computation unadjusted: production lost to the shutdown is not separated from production over which the rates were measured. The comparison therefore states what the rate change is worth on a full year at the stated volume, with the shutdown's effect on the quarterly rates left unquantified. Whether the lower rate holds over a longer run is a separate measurement; the passage states the quarter's result and the annual figure derived from it, and nothing about later quarters. The rates themselves are the project's evidence: each was measured over the quarter on the line as it ran, and the rate change is the difference between them. Stating the annual figure on the annual volume converts a quarterly rate into an annual count, and the conversion assumes the quarter's rates stand for the year. That assumption is the limit the shutdown qualifies. A quarter without a shutdown, measured on the same line, would test whether the lower rate is the line's ordinary performance or partly an artefact of the stopped period. The project as reported does not separate those two readings, and the passage does not separate them either. What the passage states is the measured change and its annual equivalent at the stated volume, bounded by the shutdown that the quarter contained.
